workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer alleges the cardholder received the Carlton armchair but it is defective: the frame wobbles, one leg is not properly seated, and the merchant has not answered the cardholder's refund request. To defend under Visa 13.3, the merchant must prove all three: (1) the published item description, (2) that the delivered item matched it, and (3) either that a return/refund route was offered and the cardholder did not use it, or that the cardholder used and kept the item after complaining.

pointers.quote:
Description: The Carlton armchair combines a hand-finished beech frame with deep-buttoned
sage velvet upholstery. Tapered solid oak legs. Seat height 46cm. Maximum recommended user
weight 120kg.
Listing snapshot generated from the product page as of 15 April 2025.

requirements.reasoning: This is a dated listing snapshot for the purchased item (SKU HH-ARM-CARL-SG, £329.00) matching the transaction date and amount.

pointers.quote: Photo taken by driver at delivery (front view only)

requirements.reasoning: The single front-view delivery photo shows a sage chair with legs, which matches colour and general form only. It cannot show frame stability or whether the legs are properly seated, which is the actual defect alleged. It also carries no SKU or serial match, no inspection or QC record, and no visible deep-button detail.

pointers.quote:
Defective items: please email returns@havenhome.example within 7 days of delivery with photos
clearly showing the defect. We will arrange a free collection and either repair, replace, or refund at
our discretion.

requirements.reasoning: The returns policy shows that a defect route exists. It does not prove the route was shown to or offered to this cardholder, or that the cardholder failed to use it. The issuer states the cardholder did request a refund and got no response, and nothing in the file rebuts that or shows the cardholder kept using the chair after complaining.

workup.action_justification: Requirement 1 is met, but requirements 2 and 3 are only partial. The merchant may be able to close both gaps with correspondence records and product condition evidence.
evidence_to_request: Full correspondence log with the cardholder, including all emails to and from returns@havenhome.example and customer service, with timestamps. This should show when the cardholder first reported the defect and whether and how the merchant responded, for example an offer of free collection, repair, replacement or refund.
Evidence that the cardholder declined or ignored an offered collection, repair or replacement, or evidence the cardholder kept and continued using the chair after complaining.
Pre-dispatch quality-control or inspection record for this unit (SKU HH-ARM-CARL-SG) confirming the frame and legs were secure, with a serial or batch number tied to the order.
Additional delivery or dispatch photos showing the legs and frame from the side and underneath, if any exist.
Order confirmation or checkout page showing the cardholder was presented with the returns and defect policy at purchase.
workup.rationale: The merchant has supplied a dated listing snapshot describing the Carlton Mid-Century Armchair in sage velvet at £329.00, which establishes the published description. The only delivery evidence is a front-view driver photo dated 18 Apr 2025, which does not show the condition of the frame or legs and so does not rebut the alleged structural fault. The returns policy describes a free-collection defect route, but there is no record that this route was offered to the cardholder, and the issuer states the cardholder's refund request went unanswered. The case cannot be represented until the merchant supplies correspondence and product condition evidence.
caveats: The issuer says the merchant did not respond to the cardholder's refund request. If the correspondence confirms this, requirement 3 cannot be met and accepting liability is likely the correct outcome.

The listing includes an 'allen key (for leg re-tightening if required during transit)'. This suggests leg loosening is a known issue that may be fixable by the cardholder. It does not by itself prove the item was not defective or that the cardholder was told how to fix it.

The delivery photo appears to be an illustrative rendering rather than a real photograph. It shows no deep-buttoning and no visible tapering of the legs, so check that it is a genuine photo of this unit.

Timing: delivery was 18 Apr 2025, so the policy's 7-day defect window ran to 25 Apr 2025. Confirm when the cardholder first reported the defect before relying on any argument that the window was missed.
The policy's 14-day 'unused, original packaging' return condition applies to change-of-mind returns and does not restrict defect claims.
AVS, CVV and 3DS results and the postcode match confirm the cardholder authorised the purchase, but they are not relevant to a not-as-described claim.

rule_text:
Visa 13.3 - Not as Described or Defective Merchandise
Issuer claim: Cardholder received the goods but they are materially not as described or defective.
Logic: ALL 3 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. The merchant's published description of the item the cardholder purchased
  2. Evidence the item delivered matches that description (photos, specs, serial number match)
  3. Evidence the merchant offered a return/refund route and the cardholder did not use it, OR evidence the cardholder used and retained the merchandise after raising the complaint
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: authenticated
Chargeback raised 23 days after the transaction
